The on-disk layout is a versioned format of this repository, specified in `SPEC.md` (draft v0.1). Anything written is little-endian and covered by a checksum. A layout change updates the SPEC, bumps a version or a feature flag, adds an ADR under `docs/adr/`, and adds a golden fixture. Segments are immutable once written.
|Container|`header.rs`, SPEC §4|Magic `PERSIA\0\x01`, format **1.0**, a 4096-byte header, two superblock slots, then frames. `format_major` 1 is the only major this build reads.|
|Segment|`segment/write.rs`, SPEC §5|Footer magic `PSEG`, format **1.0**. Sections, then the footer. `SegmentWriter` produces the bytes; `Segment::open` checks them.|
|CRC32C|`checksum.rs`|Castagnoli CRC on headers, frames, and blocks. A mismatch is `Error::Corrupt`, with the offset of the stored checksum.|
|zstd|`compress.rs`, ADR-0005|Block codec `Zstd` or `None`. Decode requires the uncompressed length the block header declared, and returns `Error::Corrupt` for any other length.|
|XXH3|`hash.rs`|XXH3-64 and XXH3-128, default secret, seed 0, for content and routing hashes. Integrity is CRC32C. Blob ids are SHA-256 (ADR-0002).|
|mmap|`mmap.rs`, ADR-0010|Read-only mapping of an immutable file range. A fault on a mapped page ends the process. Callers that cannot accept that use positioned reads.|
|`ByteSource`|`source.rs`|One buffer type for mapped, heap, and cached bytes. Clone and `slice` share the underlying `bytes::Bytes` (or the mapping) without copying the payload.|

|Unicode|`persia-analysis`, SPEC §6.3|UAX #29 word boundaries and NFKC, pinned to Unicode **17.0.0**. Built-in analyzers: `standard`, `keyword`, `whitespace`, `en`, `es`, `pt`, `fr`, `de`, `it`. Stemmers for German, English, Spanish, French, Italian, and Portuguese.|
|Fuzzing|`fuzz/fuzz_targets`, `.github/workflows/fuzz.yml`|cargo-fuzz on every target. Pull requests lint the fuzz crate. The scheduled workflow runs the targets on a dated nightly.|

Plainva follows a strict rule: **every file it writes must still open in Obsidian.** Notes are standard Markdown + YAML frontmatter; Plainva-specific presentation lives under a single namespaced `plainva:` key that other tools simply ignore. Existing vaults are never migrated or reformatted. The optional OKF conventions (typed notes, managed `index.md` files) are opt-in.

Note that the guarantee runs one way: Obsidian can always **open** what Plainva writes, but once a vault uses Plainva features (`.base` extensions such as boards or relations, managed `index.md` files), **editing** those specific files in Obsidian can break that functionality — Obsidian does not know the `plainva:` extensions. Notes without Plainva extensions can be edited anywhere, anytime. Details in the FAQ.

Plainva has no code-plugin sandbox — the vault *is* the interface. Every file is plain Markdown or YAML with an open, documented format, so any script, CLI tool or AI agent can read and write your vault directly and safely, with no Plainva-specific API to learn. See the guide's Automation & Scripts page and the machine-oriented file format reference; for AI agents there is a ready-made `AGENTS.md` template and skill. AI apps on the same computer (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, editors) can also read the vault through Plainva's read-only MCP server — no network port, folders granted per app — see Connecting AI apps. A direct write skips Plainva's pre-write backup — the version history only holds what Plainva wrote — so larger agent edits belong in a vault under Git. (A dedicated in-app plugin system remains a separate post-1.0 idea.)
